result: Viral tracing experiments identified GABAergic projections from the medial septum to the entorhinal cortex, with collaterals preferentially innervating extra-hippocampal regions (PrSd and RSg) rather than the hippocampus. Quantification showed 71% of terminals were VGAT+ and axonal branches were substantially greater in PrSd/RSg compared to hippocampal regions.
evaluation: Reviewers raised major concerns about inadequate quantification in Figure 1 experiments (Essential revision #1), stating 'this experiment lacks adequate quantification' and that claims about sparse hippocampal collaterals and VGAT immunoreactivity were 'anecdotal and requires proper quantification.' They also requested clarification on where in the EC axons terminate, noting conflicting reports in the literature about layer specificity.

result: Molecular characterization of EC-projecting neurons showed 21% were triple immunopositive for PV, SATB1, and mGluR1a, while 37.1% showed no detectable signal for these markers. PV+/SATB1+/mGluR1a- neurons did not project to EC, consistent with CA3-projecting Teevra cells.
evaluation: Reviewers requested better explanation of molecular marker significance (Essential revision #3), asking 'what does SATB1 immunoreactivity indicate in the medial septum with regard to cell classification?' and requesting clarification of which cell groups correspond to previously identified populations. The lack of clear explanation undermines confidence in the molecular characterization.

result: Eight juxtacellularly labeled neurons projecting to EC (orchid cells) exhibited rhythmic burst firing during locomotion and immobility, were immunopositive for PV/SATB1/mGluR1a, fired at theta peak, and coupled to mid-gamma oscillations. These cells innervated multiple extra-hippocampal regions, primarily PrSd.
evaluation: Reviewers raised critical concerns about selection criteria and sampling (Essential revision #2), stating 'It is unclear how many neurons (and animals) were recorded in total' and 'how the 8 labeled neurons were selected.' They noted this 'could substantially affect how one interprets the data' and questioned whether the proportion matches expected values from viral tracing. The lack of transparency about total recordings and selection criteria prevents full evaluation of these findings.

result: Detailed anatomical analysis of orchid cell TV58g showed terminals in fasciola cinereum, RSg layer 6, and extensive innervation of caudo-dorsal EC (45.6% of cortical varicosities), with no terminals in hippocampus, dentate gyrus, or PaS region.
evaluation: Reviewers questioned what happened to the 3/8 neurons that did not form collaterals in EC (Essential revision #4), indicating incomplete reporting of anatomical data. This raises concerns about selective reporting and whether the described pattern is representative of all recorded neurons.

result: Synaptic targets of orchid cells in PrSd, RSg, and FC were characterized as PV+ and nNOS+ interneurons that were SATB1+ but CCK-. Electron microscopy confirmed synaptic connections, with all 11 tested boutons forming synapses with interneurons. The axon showed target selectivity.
evaluation: Reviewers raised concerns about sample size and quantification (Essential revisions #6, #7), noting the small number of characterized neurons (13 targets from 1 cell) and requesting clarification on how many mice were used. They stated 'proper quantification is needed' for claims about target selectivity, indicating the evidence was insufficient to draw strong conclusions.

result: Orchid cells exhibited rhythmic firing across all behavioral states (locomotion, small movements, whisking/sniffing, immobility) with state-dependent differences in firing rates and burst timing. Firing rates were higher during locomotion than immobility. Putative orchid cells showed similar properties.
evaluation: Reviewers found the description unclear (Essential revisions #9, #10), asking 'What exactly does the first peak refer to?' and 'what is meant by due to state-dependent features of the spike bursts?' The introduction of 8 additional putative orchid cells raised questions about false positive/negative rates (Essential revision #8), with reviewers asking 'when these criteria are applied to all neurons with recovered axons...how many meet the criteria and don't have EC projecting axons.' This indicates concerns about classification reliability.

result: Two additional SATB1+/PV- cells with long bursts but low burst incidence projected to dentate gyrus and CA3, not EC. Teevra cells exhibited short bursts and fired at theta trough, contrasting with orchid cells. No septo-hippocampal neurons (n=15) had terminals in extra-hippocampal regions.
evaluation: Reviewers found the description of these control experiments unclear (Essential revision #11), asking 'Which ones? Do the authors mean the 2 cells that are mentioned in this subsection?' This lack of clarity, combined with concerns about classification criteria raised in Essential revision #8, undermines confidence in the reliability of distinguishing orchid cells from other cell types.

result: During locomotion, theta oscillations in CA1d and EC were in phase. During immobility, EC lacked high-power ripples during hippocampal sharp waves. Orchid cells showed non-Poisson firing rate distributions during SWRs, with some reducing firing and others showing transient increases after ripples.
evaluation: Reviewers found Figure 6 experiments 'quite confusing' (Essential revision #15), questioning whether data came from only 1 mouse and whether the 9/9 neurons were from the same animal. They also questioned 'the point of these experiments' and how they go beyond previous work from the Buzsaki lab, indicating the novelty and interpretation of these findings were unclear.

result: Stereological analysis estimated the MSDB population immunoreactive for PV, SATB1, and/or mGluR1a as 50,680 neurons. The largest group was PV-/SATB1+/mGluR1a- (37.9%), which were also the most numerous EC-projecting cells. Triple immunopositive neurons (orchid cells) represented 7.2% of the population.
evaluation: Reviewers requested that Figure 7 data be more directly compared to cell labeling data (Essential revision #16), asking 'is the proportion of triple positive neurons similar to the proportion of orchid cells in the total population of recorded MS neurons?' and whether data could be normalized to total cell populations. This indicates the relationship between the stereological counts and the functionally characterized cells was not clearly established.

result: Four behavioral states were categorized (locomotion, small movements, whisking/sniffing, immobility) based on video, wheel activity, EMG, and accelerometer. Theta oscillations dominated during locomotion and small movements, while LIA and delta oscillations emerged during whisking/sniffing and immobility.
evaluation: Reviewers did not raise concerns about the behavioral state classification methods or the characterization of network states. These methodological details appear to have been accepted without challenge.
